title: [F.] Sánchez to 'José González' (identified as Félix Díaz), 12 January 1922 (catalogue 1445, CEHM-Carso DCXXI.3.323.1): cipher words in the Gronsfeld key 313 that Narváez published for the Wellington letter, deciphered

steps.what: Two page images fetched from visor.cehm.org.mx (plain http), 1.6 s apart, no login.
11 runs (32 cipher words) transcribed from the full pages and again from crops for most runs.
Narváez's key 313 for the Wellington letter applied unchanged (restart per word); key 103, which the letter says was dropped, also tried: no sense.

The key was not built from this letter, so the whole letter is held out: 22 of 32 cipher words exact, 177 of 185 letters (95.7%) in the 29 identified words; the misses are typing slips (shift off the cycle late in long words). The deciphered signature (Sánchez), the clear mention of key 313, and two names that recur in clear in the CEHM summary of DCXXI.3.330.1 (Landeros, El Látigo) agree.
Runs decrypted mechanically and read with every departure marked; check_marks.py passes. 32 words: 22 verbatim, 7 repaired, 3 holes. Dan's _check_reading.py: reading 0.50, translation 0.80.
Narváez 2015 read; CEHM summaries of neighbouring records checked.

Independent blind review by an AI language-model agent separate from the solver: 6 of 11 runs copied from its own crops, 0 disagreements; key checked in Narváez 2015; W07, W09 and W10 decoded by hand, exact; check_marks.py re-run (passes). Applied after the review: the pencil note at the foot of p. 2 recorded as a partial gloss, '[? Emilio]' corrected to '[Emilio]', W06 offered as [?Baja] in the sentences (still counted as a hole). Dan's _check_reading.py on 13 Nov 2026 after these changes: reading 0.46 (23 of 50 sentences), translation 0.773 (17 of 22).

Integration check by the repository: check_marks.py reproduced (22 verbatim, 7 repaired, 3 holes of 32 words); own decoder from the rule (key 313, restart per word) gives the same decryption of all 11 runs; CEHM images 0001 and 0002 compared with the transcription, all 11 runs agree. Narváez 2015 not read by the integrating session. Class read in part (68.8%) stands.

validation.notes: A Gronsfeld-type key (shift by position in the word) is not a letter-to-value table, so the token-by-token n-gram validation does not apply; the key is a published one (Narváez 2015) applied unchanged to a whole letter, with 177 of 185 letters of the identified words exact.

texts.label: [F.] Sánchez to 'José González', 12 Jan 1922: 11 cipher runs
texts.summary: General Landeros has died in the district of Huejotzingo; the friends agree to group together to 'nombrar una junta'; a newspaper, 'El Látigo', is to be printed in neighbouring Tlaxcala; Figueroa had an incident in Veracruz; an act came from the Mixteca of Oaxaca; greetings from Miguel Gutiérrez Goitia, Manuel Márquez, Arturo Osorio, Rodolfo Urdapilleta, Francisco Machorro and a Lic. [?]; cover address Sr. Manuel [?], Plazuela Parral # 1, Puebla; signed F. Sánchez.
texts.note: Not prose: 11 runs (names, a place, a newspaper title and one three-word phrase) in a letter in clear Spanish, each given in its clear sentence with an English translation. Words: 32 cipher words, 22 verbatim from the signs (68.8%), 7 with a marked repair, 0 from a gloss, 3 holes (VAIA, YULAS, CORCU).

reading_review.note: The key holds and the runs read in their clear sentences: 6 of 9 context sentences without holes, the other 3 with one hole each; 3 holes and 7 marked repairs in 32 cipher words.

gaps.detail: One occurrence. The reviewer suggests 'Baja' (the Mixteca Baja of Oaxaca); with the third shift 2 instead of 3 the word gives VAJA. Offered as [?Baja], counted as a hole.
One occurrence; no single-shift change gives a name we can confirm.

gaps.item: W10 'fpufv' (CORCU), the surname in the cover address
gaps.detail: The pencil note at the foot of p. 2 that seems to decode this address ('Manuel Co/Ro z[a]...') is overwritten at the surname.

gaps.item: Pen strokes over letters in W07 (xf, uu, lw, ut)
gaps.detail: Perhaps a reader's marks; not interpreted. The typed letters under them decode to names.

prior.where: CEHM: 'incluye claves no descifradas'. Narváez 2015 publishes the key 313 for DCXXI.6.588.1 and does not discuss this letter (full text read 12 Nov 2026).

human: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 1445) and the rules; AI language-model agents transcribed, applied the published key, read and checked. No target-specific human intervention. No human palaeographer checked the text.
